issues.legal_issue: On the death of a tenant, the succeeding heirs hold the tenancy as joint tenants in relation to the landlord, rather than as tenants-in-common.
material_facts: The premises were let jointly to the deceased tenant and another tenant.
After the deceased tenant died, one of his heirs succeeded to the tenancy; the other original joint tenant remained a tenant.
The dispute arose in eviction proceedings concerning the premises.
issues.conclusion: The heirs inherited the tenancy as joint tenants. The tenancy remained a single tenancy and was not divided into separate tenancies among the heirs.
issues.legal_principle: Under H.C. Pandey v. G.C. Paul, on the death of the original tenant the tenancy devolves as a single tenancy on the heirs, who succeed as joint tenants as between themselves and the landlord. Section 19 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, which provides for heirs to take as tenants-in-common, concerns the rights of heirs inter se and does not determine their relationship with a landlord, as explained in Mst. Surayya Begum v. Mohd. Usman. The Court also relied on the principles in Boddu Venkatakrishna Rao v. Smt. Boddu Satyavathi, Gian Devi Anand v. Jeevan Kumar, Mohd. Usman v. (Mst.) Surayya Begum, and Harish Tandon v. Addl. District Magistrate.

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: The landlord brought proceedings seeking eviction from rented premises.
predicates.premises_jointly_let: The premises were let to the deceased tenant together with another tenant.
predicates.original_tenant_died_leaving_heirs: The original tenant died and left heirs who succeeded to the tenancy.

issues.definition: When rented premises were jointly let, the original tenant died leaving heirs, and the dispute arises in eviction proceedings, the heirs hold the tenancy as joint tenants in relation to the landlord.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord may obtain an eviction decree by impleading an occupying joint tenant without impleading every heir, and the decree binds the joint tenants.
material_facts: An eviction decree was obtained after one of the tenants was a party to the proceedings; another heir of the deceased tenant was not impleaded.
The omitted heir objected during execution, claiming an interest in and possession of the premises.
The objector produced only two old rent receipts as evidence of possession and acknowledged a dispute with the other tenant and that they had parted ways.
issues.conclusion: It was sufficient to implead an occupying joint tenant; the landlord was not required to implead every heir, whether or not they occupied the premises. The eviction decree bound all joint tenants, and the omitted heir’s objection failed.
issues.legal_principle: Because the tenancy inherited by the heirs is a single joint tenancy, occupation by one joint tenant is occupation on behalf of all, and an eviction petition against one joint tenant is sufficient to bind all. The landlord need not implead every heir, including heirs not occupying the premises. The Court applied H.C. Pandey v. G.C. Paul and its conclusion that the tenancy does not split into separate tenancies among the heirs.

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: The landlord brought proceedings seeking eviction from rented premises.
predicates.inherited_tenancy_is_single: The heirs succeeded to one undivided tenancy rather than separate tenancies.
predicates.at_least_one_occupying_joint_tenant_is_n: The landlord included at least one joint tenant who occupied the premises as a party to the eviction proceedings.

issues.definition: In eviction proceedings concerning a single inherited tenancy, naming an occupying joint tenant is sufficient for the resulting decree to bind all joint tenants.
